title: Finite evaluation of canonical identity-open cancellation
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$, a coefficient datum $C$ with prime $\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ as in [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Let $o$ be the simultaneous coefficient-system operations of [def-sf-integral-system-operations], and $z$ their realization data with canonical section-normalized bridge [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge]. For every scheme $W$, integer $m\ge0$, and arbitrary derived coefficient system $M$ on $W$, let $e_W:J_{\mathrm{id}_W}\simeq\mathrm{id}$ be openIdentity of [def-sf-integral-proper-projection-coordinates], let $\operatorname{ev}_m$ be finite evaluation, let $\epsilon_{J,m}$ be the specified open-evaluation comparison, and let $e_{W,m}:j_{\mathrm{id}_W,!}\simeq\mathrm{id}$ be the intrinsic finite identity-open comparison normalized by its open-adjunction unit. Then $\operatorname{ev}_m(e_W(M))=\epsilon_{J,m}(M)\mathbin{\gg} e_{W,m}(\operatorname{ev}_m M)$, where the displayed composite is in diagrammatic order. There is no integral object, support construction, or six-functor operation datum in this identity.

proof.text: Use systemPushIdentityPullUnit to obtain the normalized system pullback identity e, with its two-identity compositor unit equation. Its conjugate identifies e with the canonical bridge pull comparison followed by SemilinearProperOpen.pId. Adjoint uniqueness, applied after transport of the right adjoint, therefore identifies the system identity-open cancellation with leftAdjointIdIso for e.

proof.text: Transport the ordinary upperStarComp_id_left law through the intrinsic module realization equivalence, using its unit and counit triangle identity. Localize the resulting identity with descend_left_unit to obtain the unit law for the finite intrinsic derived pullback compositor. Apply systemPullbackCompositorEvaluation to the pair of identity scheme maps. For any functors P,Q isomorphic to identities and comparison q:P V -> V Q, composition compatibility forces q followed by the Q identity comparison to equal V of the P identity comparison: substitute the two compositor unit laws, use naturality of q on the P identity comparison, cancel q at P(M), and use faithfulness of Q, which is isomorphic to the identity. This uses no faithfulness of finite evaluation.

proof.text: The unit equation for the inverse mate specified by OpenEvaluation.transpose gives V(eta) followed by q equal to the finite open unit followed by finite pullback of inverse open evaluation. Postcompose with the finite pullback identity comparison and use Step 2. Naturality of that identity comparison identifies the result with inverse finite identity-open cancellation followed by inverse open evaluation. The leftAdjointIdIso inverse formula identifies the other side with evaluation of inverse system cancellation. Invert this equality. The proved generic exact_left_id_localized lemma identifies the finite leftAdjointIdIso with mapDerivedCategoryNatIso(sfIntrinsicOpenId) followed by mapDerivedCategoryIdIso, giving exactly the required equality at M.

theorem systemIdentityOpenEvaluation
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} {C : D.CoefficientDatum}
    {E : Type u} [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E]
    (o : Operations C.l E) (z : Realizations C.l E D o)
    (W : Scheme.{u}) (m : ℕ) (M : System C.l E W) :
    (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation C.l E W m).map
        ((openIdentity o z W).hom.app M) =
      ((o.openEvaluation (𝟙 W)).evaluation m).hom.app M ≫
        (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso
          (@sfIntrinsicOpenId (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E (m + 1)) _
            (Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing C.l E (m + 1)
              (Nat.le_add_left 1 m)) W) ≪≫
          Functor.mapDerivedCategoryIdIso _).hom.app
            ((coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation C.l E W m).obj M)
